findings.title: First-time installations bypass the GitHub-user check
findings.body: When no `Integration` exists yet for this installation ID, this branch advances the pipeline without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installation sender. A first-time GitHub App installation commonly reaches this path if its installation webhook has not yet created the Integration, so an authenticated GitHub account different from the installer can complete setup despite the security check. Validate the installer identity on this path too, or ensure the comparison is performed against trusted installation data before completing setup.

findings.title: Missing sender metadata causes an unhandled KeyError
findings.body: This assumes every existing Integration has `metadata['sender']['login']`. Integrations created before this check was introduced, or integrations whose sender metadata was not recorded, can lack either key. Reinstalling such an installation reaches this line and raises `KeyError`, returning a server error instead of the intended invalid-installation response. Treat missing or malformed sender metadata as a failed validation and return the normal error response.
